record.paper_title: Bounded compact and dual compact approximation properties of Hardy spaces: new results and open problems
record.context_brief: Sharper DCAP bounds for Hardy-Lorentz spaces
record.original_question: For the Hardy-Lorentz space H[L^{p,q}] with 1 < q ≤ p < ∞, find a nontrivial lower bound for the dual compact approximation constant M*(H[L^{p,q}]) and improve the upper bound M*(H[L^{p,q}]) ≤ 2 given in equation (5.10).

evidence.quote: Open problem 5.8. (b) Let 1 < q ≤ p < ∞. Find a nontrivial lower bound for M∗(H[Lp,q]). Improve the upper bound for M∗(H[Lp,q]) given by (5.10).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ be a complex Banach space. A bounded linear operator $T:X\to X$ is called compact if it maps the unit ball of $X$ to a relatively compact subset of $X$. The Banach space $X$ is said to have the dual compact approximation property (DCAP) if there exists a constant $C\ge 1$ and a net (or sequence, in the separable case) $(T_\alpha)$ of bounded linear operators on $X$ such that:
(i) each adjoint $T_\alpha^*:X^*\to X^*$ is compact,
(ii) $\sup_\alpha \|T_\alpha\| \le C$, and
(iii) $T_\alpha x \to x$ for every $x\in X$.
The dual compact approximation constant $M^*(X)$ is the infimum of all such $C\ge 1$ for which such a net exists (and $M^*(X)=\infty$ if no such net exists).

For $1<p<\infty$ and $1\le q<\infty$, the Lorentz space $L^{p,q}(\mathbb{T})$ on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$ (with normalized Lebesgue measure) consists of all measurable functions $f$ on $\mathbb{T}$ for which
$$\|f\|_{p,q} \;=\; \Bigl(\int_0^\infty \bigl(t^{1/p} f^*(t)\bigr)^q \frac{dt}{t}\Bigr)^{1/q} < \infty,$$
where $f^*$ is the nonincreasing rearrangement of $|f|$. The Hardy–Lorentz space $H[L^{p,q}]$ is defined as the closed subspace of $L^{p,q}(\mathbb{T})$ consisting of functions $f$ whose Fourier coefficients $\hat f(n)$ vanish for all integers $n<0$.

It is known that for $1<q\le p<\infty$ one has the upper bound
$$M^*(H[L^{p,q}]) \;\le\; 2.$$

Problem. Let $1<q\le p<\infty$. 
(a) Establish a nontrivial lower bound $M^*(H[L^{p,q}]) \ge c(p,q) > 1$.
(b) Improve the upper bound $M^*(H[L^{p,q}]) \le 2$ (for instance, to a bound of the form $2|1-2/r|$ for some appropriate exponent $r=r(p,q)$, or to any constant strictly less than $2$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a nontrivial lower bound and a sharper upper bound for the dual compact approximation constant $M^*(H[L^{p,q}])$ of Hardy–Lorentz spaces is stated as an open problem in recent work on bounded compact and dual compact approximation properties of Hardy spaces. No published resolution was found; only the upper bound $\le 2$ (and sharper estimates in the classical $L^p$ case, $M^*(H^p)\le 2|1-2/p|$) is available.

status_evidence.title: Bounded compact and dual compact approximation properties of Hardy spaces: new results and open problems - King's College London
status_evidence.snippet: For classical weighted Hardy spaces H^p(w) with 1<p<∞: M(H^p(w))≤2|1−2/p| and M*(H^p(w))≤2|1−2/p|; for reflexive Hardy spaces H[X(w)], M*(H[X(w)])≤2. Hardy-Lorentz constants are treated and listed among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The improvement of the bound M*(H[L^{p,q}])≤2 and a nontrivial lower bound are listed as open problems.
